Time series data is a sequence of data points in which insights are gained by analyzing changes over time.

In a regular collection, data is stored sequentially as blocks on disk, optimizing write speed. However, it requires one index for each data point, which quickly grows very large. It also requires a second index that contains the time series identifier and timestamps themselves, so that users can query for a single series. To read this data, MongoDB has to process all of the database and disk blocks that contain it, even if a block only contains a single relevant document.

MongoDB automatically enables block processing for eligible time series queries. You cannot manually specify whether a query uses block processing. Block processing is automatic. Users cannot enable or disable it for a single query. Eligibility is decided per query, and queries with unsupported operators or expressions run on the classic engine. SBE support is version specific and still changing.

For time series collections, TTL indexes also remove a bucket of data when all documents inside it expire. This is equal to the upper timestamp limit of the bucket, plus the `expireAfterSeconds` value. For example, if a bucket covers data up until `2023-03-27T18:29:59Z` and `expireAfterSeconds` is 300, the TTL index expires the bucket after `2023-03-27T18:34:59Z`.

If MongoDB cannot obtain the sort order with an index scan, then MongoDB uses a top-k sort algorithm. This algorithm buffers the first `k` results (or last, depending on the sort order) seen so far by the underlying index or collection access. If the memory footprint of these `k` results exceeds 100 megabytes, MongoDB automatically writes temporary files to disk unless the query specifies [`cursor.allowDiskUse()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowdiskuse.md#mongodb-method-cursor.allowDiskUse) with a value of `false` (in which case, the query fails).

Delta Encoding takes advantage of the data in your time series collection having time-series characteristics. Instead of storing absolute values, Delta Encoding assumes that the measurements will not change rapidly between each other. This approach reduces the amount of information required by only storing the difference between measurements.

Starting in version 8.0, MongoDB may execute certain time series queries using block processing. This performance improvement processes queries in "blocks" of data, rather than individual values. Block processing improves query execution speed and throughput when working with time series collections.

Time series collections use [zstd](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-zstd) compression, which differs from the global default compression algorithm, [snappy.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-snappy)

MongoDB does not create an index on the `_id` field when you create a time series collection. This differs from regular collections which have an index on the `_id` field by default. Commands that specify a hint on the `_id` field on time series collections return an error unless you manually create an index on the `_id` field.

The SBE reference page says SBE is disabled automatically on collections that have an index with a hashed-field prefix followed by a non-hashed field, with both fields in the index. Ineligible queries fall back to the classic engine. The page does not tie this rule to time series specifically.

Collection data in the WiredTiger cache is uncompressed, so block compression saves disk but not cache space; the OS filesystem cache holds the compressed on-disk form. Indexes in cache still benefit from prefix compression. Compressed time series storage size therefore understates the cache footprint of hot buckets.

MongoDB's docs state a bucket holds at most 1000 measurements or 125 KiB, whichever is lower, and MongoDB may enforce a lower maximum for high-cardinality data so the working set of buckets fits in the WiredTiger cache.

- Divides the time for the [`$dateTrunc`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-dateTrunc) calculation into [binSize](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#std-label-dateTrunc-binSize) time periods in the specified time [unit.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#std-label-dateTrunc-unit)

- A string other than `week`, [`$dateTrunc`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-dateTrunc) uses a reference date of `2000-01-01T00:00:00.00Z`. For example, if [binSize](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#std-label-dateTrunc-binSize) is `10` and [unit](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#std-label-dateTrunc-unit) is `year`, example time periods are:

- Equal to `week`, [`$dateTrunc`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-dateTrunc) uses a reference date that is set to the earliest first day of the week that is greater than or equal to `2000-01-01`. The first day is set using [startOfWeek](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#std-label-dateTrunc-startOfWeek) (the default is Sunday).

- `year`: [`$dateTrunc`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-dateTrunc) returns the [ISODate](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-ISODate) for the start of January 1 for the year in [date.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#std-label-dateTrunc-date)

- `quarter`: [`$dateTrunc`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-dateTrunc) returns the [ISODate](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-ISODate) for the start of the first day of the calendar quarter in [date.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#std-label-dateTrunc-date)

- `month`: [`$dateTrunc`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-dateTrunc) returns the [ISODate](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-ISODate) for the start of the first day of the month in [date.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#std-label-dateTrunc-date)

- `day`: [`$dateTrunc`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-dateTrunc) returns the [ISODate](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-ISODate) for the start of the day in [date.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#std-label-dateTrunc-date)

- `hour`: [`$dateTrunc`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-dateTrunc) returns the [ISODate](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-ISODate) for the start of the hour in [date.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#std-label-dateTrunc-date)

- `minute`: [`$dateTrunc`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-dateTrunc) returns the [ISODate](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-ISODate) for the start of the minute in [date.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#std-label-dateTrunc-date)

- `second`: [`$dateTrunc`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-dateTrunc) returns the [ISODate](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-ISODate) for start of the second in [date.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#std-label-dateTrunc-date)

- Specified: [`$dateTrunc`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-dateTrunc) uses [startOfWeek](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#std-label-dateTrunc-startOfWeek) as the first day of the week for the calculation.
- Omitted: [`$dateTrunc`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/datetrunc.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-dateTrunc) uses Sunday as the start of the week for the calculation.
